title: System identification campaign - Skywalker X8 UAV
access: Full public access to DataverseNO Version 1.0 under CC0 1.0 Universal, including metadata, README, 35 files, and direct unauthenticated datafile endpoints. The course contract pins DOI 10.18710/U4TLYV, Version 1.0, and per-file MD5 checksums; retrieved 2026-08-06.
topics: Version 1.0 dataset organization: 17 independent maneuvers, with 13 creator-designated training records and four creator-designated validation records.
Longitudinal teaching subset: seven training and two validation CSVs spanning 3211 elevator sequences and elevator doublets.
Record contract: headerless 41-column numeric CSVs at nominal 40 Hz; each maneuver starts at sample index zero and time zero and must retain its own boundary.
Acquisition contract: STIM300 IMU downsampled from 200 Hz, GPS and propulsion upsampled from 10 Hz, commands originally 40 Hz, with manual synchronization before the released 40 Hz records.
Teaching channels: time, elevator command, pitch angular rate, estimated pitch and pitch rate, vertical velocity, angle of attack, and airspeed fields with README-specified SI units.
key_results: The nine longitudinal files contain 3,828 complete rows with no missing values in the scout's structural audit and a nominal sample interval of 0.025 s.

The primary proposed input is elevator command (column 2, rad) and the primary proposed response is IMU pitch angular rate `IMU_angvel_q` (column 9, rad/s); alternate outputs must be declared before fitting.
Creator-designated validation maneuvers are `validation/longitudinal_3211_5.csv` and `validation/longitudinal_doublet_4.csv`; they are not a random or final-percentage split.
Strong northwesterly wind and manual multirate synchronization are stated threats to fixed-coefficient and exact-delay interpretations.
No model order, coefficient, residual metric, or performance threshold is a repository result; every such value must be computed by a deterministic course artifact after the pipeline is frozen.
pedagogy: Use the source as a measured record contract rather than as a prevalidated model. Learners first verify checksums, columns, units, time steps, and maneuver boundaries; they then select a low-order AR/ARX protocol on creator-designated training files and evaluate both untouched longitudinal validation maneuvers with state reset at each boundary.
figures: Draw the creator-designated seven-training/two-validation maneuver partition, separating 3211 and doublet excitation and making record-boundary resets visible.
After deterministic computation exists, draw residuals by time and validation maneuver for a declared baseline and one frozen low-order elevator-to-pitch-rate model.
Draw the acquisition-to-validation pipeline with manual synchronization/resampling marked as a limitation on delay inference.
gems: Two validation excitation families permit a direct test of whether residual structure changes between a 3211 sequence and a doublet without inventing a stall-region label.
Every maneuver restarts at n=0 and t=0, making a false cross-file lag transition an unusually clear leakage and bookkeeping counterexample.
The released 40 Hz table merges channels originally sampled at 200, 40, and 10 Hz, so an apparently clean one-sample lag cannot be equated automatically with physical actuator delay.

Column names, units, sample convention, maneuver names, and synchronization → Version 1.0 README.
Training-only fitting → seven longitudinal CSVs under interoperability_files/training.
